clue.text: Fairly good communicating, including good detail ultimately

parts.note: something fairly good is fine-ish, written here as one word in its usual spelling

indicators.note: including means the phrase for communicating holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: people communicating are in touch

explanation.surface: A school report praising fairly good communication skills, with attention to detail at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening piece only works if you say it as 'fine-ish'; the setter spells it as the everyday word it sounds like. 'Communicating' is not a skill being graded but being in contact.
explanation.definitionFit: The last small detail added to complete a piece of work is its final polish or last touch.

clue.text: As a result of poor sort of path, men sent half in the wrong direction

parts.note: from means as a result of, as in 'tired from work'
bad means poor in quality
a tow-path is a sort of path along a canal, so tow is the qualifier
OR, other ranks, is the usual abbreviation for soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: half means only the first half of the word sent is used

explanation.surface: A poor hiking route leads a party of men off the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: TOW is the kind of path, as in towpath; OR (other ranks) is crossword shorthand for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Going steadily from one poor state to a poorer one is heading the wrong way, deteriorating.

clue.text: There's a tiny bit of queen in sister

indicators.note: in means the queen's name goes inside the word for sister

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
Cleo is short for Cleopatra, queen of Egypt

explanation.surface: A small sign of royalty is detected in a woman's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sister' is a nun here, not a sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: A nucleon is a proton or neutron, a particle in an atomic nucleus, so a very small piece of matter.

clue.text: Firm got money for employing one

indicators.note: employing means using, here taking in and holding the number one

parts.note: if you got money for something, you sold it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A company earned money by hiring someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' is not the company but the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid means firm, hard and not giving way when pressed.

clue.text: One local man caught cold, not working

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: caught means the local man has grabbed the letter for cold and holds it

parts.note: a native is someone from the local area
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A local man has caught a cold and is off work.
explanation.definitionFit: Inactive means idle or not operating, which is what not working describes.

clue.text: Lacking character, holding as ingratiating

indicators.note: holding means the word for dull is wrapped around the little word as

parts.note: grey means dull and featureless, lacking character

explanation.surface: Someone characterless trying to win favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking character' looks like the definition; it is the colourless word that 'holding' wraps round the two-letter piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy can describe a manner that is oily and unctuous, trying to curry favour.

clue.text: Colour is replaced here immediately

definitions.meaning: in snooker a potted coloured ball is put back on its own marked spot on the table
immediately means at once, without delay

explanation.walkthrough: SNOOKER is a cue game on a table with coloured balls; each colour has its own spot to which it is returned after being potted, until the closing stages.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dealt with at once, right where you are, is the idiom for doing something without delay.

clue.text: Cruel, so to manipulate end of debate

indicators.note: to manipulate means the letters of the fodder are handled and moved into a new order

explanation.surface: A cruel tactic used to cut short an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to manipulate' rearranges CRUEL and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament a closure is a procedure that ends a debate and forces a vote.

clue.text: Shocking pastoral events?

indicators.note: shocking suggests the letters jolted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Disturbing happenings out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shocking' rearranges PASTORAL EVENTS, and the whole clue also describes the 1381 uprising of English farm workers.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1381 rising of English rural workers against the poll tax was a startling rustic upheaval.

clue.text: Turned very worried, going to block or to swing

indicators.note: going to here means the block is going into the middle of the other letters
turned means the word for very is flipped round so it reads backwards

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so tired'
ate means worried, as in 'what's eating you?' in the past tense
a cill (also spelt sill) is the block of stone or wood at the foot of a window or door

explanation.surface: Someone who turned very anxious can't decide whether to block something or let it swing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned' flips the word for very; CILL is a variant spelling of sill. 'Block' is both the piece and part of the placing instruction 'going to', a looseness the blog's commenters noted.
explanation.definitionFit: To oscillate is to move to and fro regularly like a pendulum, which is what swinging means.

clue.text: Pin makes initially tiny perforation

indicators.note: initially means take only the first letter of the word tiny

parts.note: a perforation is a hole punched through something

explanation.surface: A pin is said to make a very small perforation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thole is a pin set in a boat's gunwale to act as a fulcrum for an oar.

clue.text: Mix up book —- what library does

parts.note: a library's job is to lend books to its members

explanation.surface: Someone muddles up a book, then describes a library's function.
explanation.definitionFit: To blend is to mix things together thoroughly, a synonym of mixing up.

clue.text: Parts of body designed to receive smacks

definitions.text: Parts of body designed to receive smacks

parts.words: Parts of body designed to receive smacks
parts.note: smacks suggests slaps, as if the body parts were made to be hit, but a smack is also a taste or flavour, as in 'smacks of garlic'

explanation.definitionFit: The small sense organs on the tongue are what detect flavours, the 'smacks' of the clue.

clue.text: Gift available in case

indicators.note: in means the word for available goes inside the grammatical case

parts.note: the dative is a grammatical case, used for the indirect object
on means available, as in 'is the offer still on?'

explanation.surface: A present is available inside a box or case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a box to put the gift in; it is the grammatical case, DATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A donative is a formal gift or donation, especially an official one.

clue.text: Time big beast replaced worker with one that is a communicator

indicators.note: replaced ... with means the worker's letters are swapped out for one's

parts.note: an elephant is a very big beast
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: A powerful figure, the big beast, swaps a worker for someone who can talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big beast' sounds like a political heavyweight but is a literal animal; 'replaced' swaps the insect worker out of its name for the clue's 'one'.
explanation.definitionFit: A telephone is a device for communicating over a distance.

clue.text: Place in area of church with new organ

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for place sits inside the church area

parts.note: a see is the area under a bishop's authority, a diocese
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A church acquires a new organ and must find a place for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the church's musical instrument; it is a body organ.
explanation.definitionFit: The spleen is an organ of the body, lying near the stomach, that filters the blood.

clue.text: One patrolling reported pimp about to run

indicators.note: reported means the word for pimp is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a pander is a pimp, from Pandarus
CA, circa, means about
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone on patrol has heard of a pimp about to make a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A PANDA CAR is British slang for a small police patrol car, once painted in panda-like black and white or blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: A police patrol car is a vehicle used for patrolling the streets.

clue.text: Everyone remains bad, given drugs thus?

annotationWithheld.why: Everyone remains bad, given drugs thus? (6): a reverse clue, O + RALLY read as 'nobody recovers' = 'everyone remains bad'; the reading names no clue word, so reverse() is refused (reversePhrase) and cd() is refused as a downgrade
annotationWithheld.clue: Everyone remains bad, given drugs thus?

clue.text: Insect crushed in talon

indicators.note: crushed suggests the letters squashed into a new shape

explanation.surface: An insect is crushed in a bird's talon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crushed' rearranges IN TALON.
explanation.definitionFit: An antlion is an insect whose larvae dig pits to trap ants.

clue.text: Light-hearted, lacking energy to be quarrelsome

indicators.note: lacking means one letter, the symbol for energy, is taken away

parts.note: facetious means flippant or light-heartedly jokey
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone who loses their light-hearted energy turns argumentative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' takes the E out of FACETIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Factious means given to forming factions and dissent, hence contentious or quarrelsome.

clue.text: Plant hides good view

indicators.note: hides means the plant holds the word for good concealed inside it

parts.note: an onion is a plant
pi, short for pious, means good

explanation.surface: A plant conceals a fine view.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is crossword shorthand for good.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view one holds about something.

clue.text: Doctor, I come from an Italian family

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor explains his ancestry from Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Medici were the powerful Florentine banking dynasty of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Scattered troupes are struggling these days

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters of troupes thrashing about into a new order

parts.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Theatre companies are dispersed and having a hard time in the present climate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges TROUPES into OUTSPRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Outspread means spread out or extended widely, so laid out in a scattered way.

clue.text: Very old and sweet tenor, say

parts.note: an ice, such as an ice lolly or ice cream, is a sweet treat

explanation.surface: Praise for a singer: a very old tenor who still sounds sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' looks like the singer described; with 'say' it is an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is one type of singing voice, alongside bass, baritone, alto and soprano.

clue.text: Through the night, one kept right away from poet

indicators.note: away from means the letter for right is removed from the poet's name

parts.note: Virgil was the Roman poet of the Aeneid

explanation.surface: Someone sat up all night and kept their right to stay away from a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from VIRGIL gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a watch kept through the night, staying awake to guard or pray.

clue.text: County fielder to drop back: move!

indicators.note: drop back means the back letter of the fielder's position is dropped

parts.note: slip is a cricket fielding position beside the wicketkeeper
go means move, as in 'get going'

explanation.surface: A cricket captain tells a fielder to drop deeper and get moving.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGO is a county in the north-west of Ireland. 'drop back' removes the last letter of SLIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Isn't it common to seize pawn, nothing disguised?

indicators.note: to seize means the slang word grabs the pawn, holding it in its middle

parts.note: innit is a slang, socially 'common', form of isn't it
a cog, as in a cog in the machine, is a minor figure used by others, like a pawn
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A chess question: is it vulgar to take a pawn while giving nothing away?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Isn't it common' is not a question but a definition: INNIT, a slang form of 'isn't it'. Pawn is not the chess piece but a person used as a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone travelling incognito conceals their identity, so is disguised.

clue.text: From Alpine frontier, recollected a warmer world

indicators.note: recollected suggests the letters gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller remembers somewhere warmer from a trip to an Alpine border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges ALPINE FRONTIER. 'Recollected' looks like remembered.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury and Venus orbit inside Earth's orbit, closer to the sun, so they are generally hotter worlds.
